title: Basilicata's Fuel Prices Hold Steady, But Metano Is Quietly Breaking From the National Trend
dek: While Benzina and Gasolio track Italy's post-peak pullback closely, Basilicata's Metano has fallen for three straight weeks even as the national average keeps climbing.
executive_summary: On October 11, Basilicata's self-service prices stood at €2.082/L for Benzina, €2.290/L for Gasolio, €0.786/L for GPL, and €1.799/kg for Metano. Day over day, nothing moved much — Benzina and Gasolio ticked up by roughly a tenth of a cent or less, while GPL and Metano held dead flat. Against the national self-service averages for the same day (€2.047, €2.275, €0.773, and €1.867 respectively), Basilicata is running a small premium on three of the four fuels — about 1.7% above Italy on Benzina and GPL, 0.7% above on Gasolio — but it is the cheaper story on Metano, sitting 3.6% below the national average.

Zoom out to the twelve weeks of data tracked since 2026-07-21 (ISO weeks 2026-W30 through 2026-W41), and the most interesting pattern is a fuel-by-fuel split between Basilicata and the rest of the country. Metano is the clearest divergence: the national self-service average has climbed in every one of the last eleven weeks, up 22.7% since late July with no sign of topping out, while Basilicata's own Metano price peaked back in mid-September (weeks W38-W39) and has since fallen for three straight weeks, down 7.2% off that peak. GPL tells a smaller but sharper version of the same story — Basilicata's GPL price dropped 2.9% in a single week (W37 to W38) and has sat flat ever since, for a net -3.5% since late July, while the national GPL average actually rose 1.4% over the same stretch. Benzina and Gasolio, by contrast, have moved roughly in lockstep with the rest of Italy: both regional and national prices rose through August and September to a late-September peak, then pulled back by early October.

fuel_sections.heading: Benzina Steadies Just Above the National Average
paragraphs: Basilicata's self-service Benzina price was €2.082/L on October 11, essentially unchanged from €2.081/L the day before (+0.02%). That keeps it about 1.7% above the national self-service average of €2.047/L, a premium that has held fairly steady through the recent slide.

Over the twelve tracked weeks, Basilicata's weekly Benzina average rose from €1.987 in W30 to a peak of €2.180 in W39 (mid-September), a 9.7% climb, before pulling back to €2.081 by W41 — a 4.5% retreat from the peak. Nationally the pattern was almost identical in shape but slightly smaller in both directions: the national weekly average rose from €1.976 in W30 to €2.167 in W39 (also +9.7%) and has since fallen 5.5% to €2.048 by W41. The net effect is that Basilicata's overall rise since late July (+4.7%) slightly outpaces the national rise (+3.7%), even though its pullback from the peak has been a touch gentler than the rest of Italy's.

fuel_sections.heading: Diesel Pulls Back From a Late-September Spike, Slower Than the Rest of Italy
paragraphs: Gasolio's self-service price in Basilicata was €2.290/L on October 11, up slightly from €2.289/L the previous day (+0.07%). That is about 0.7% above the national self-service average of €2.275/L — a narrower gap than Benzina's.

The multi-week pattern mirrors Benzina but with a sharper swing: Basilicata's weekly Gasolio average rose from €2.179 in W30 to a peak of €2.372 in W39, a 5.1% climb, before easing back 3.4% to €2.291 by W41. Nationally, the climb was similar in size (from €2.175 in W30 to €2.374 in W39, +4.9%) but the pullback since the peak has been a bit deeper, down 3.9% to €2.281 by W41. So while Basilicata's diesel rose slightly faster into the September peak, it has also been slightly stickier on the way back down — a pattern that, if it continues, would widen Basilicata's premium over the national average in the coming weeks.

fuel_sections.heading: GPL's One-Week September Plunge Still Separates Basilicata From the National Trend
paragraphs: GPL's self-service price in Basilicata was €0.786/L on October 11, unchanged from the day before. That is about 1.7% above the national self-service average of €0.773/L.

GPL is the fuel where Basilicata has moved in the opposite direction from the rest of Italy. Its weekly average fell from €0.814 in W30 to €0.786 by W41, a net -3.5%, with almost the entire move concentrated in a single week: W37 to W38, when it dropped 2.9% from €0.810 to €0.786, then sat flat for the four weeks since. The national GPL average took the opposite path, rising 1.4% over the same stretch, from €0.759 in W30 to €0.770 by W41. That divergence — one sudden regional repricing against a slow national rise — is the sharpest fuel-level split in this report.

fuel_sections.heading: Metano Splits Hard: National Prices Keep Climbing, Basilicata Pulls Back for a Third Week
paragraphs: Metano's self-service price in Basilicata was €1.799/kg on October 11, flat day over day. That keeps it notably cheaper than the rest of Italy — about 3.6% below the national self-service average of €1.867/kg, the only one of the four fuels where Basilicata undercuts the national price.

This is the report's clearest divergence. Basilicata's weekly Metano average rose from €1.550/kg in W31 to a peak of €1.939/kg across W38 and W39 (+25.1%), then reversed, falling for three straight weeks to €1.799 by W41 — down 7.2% from the peak. The national average took a completely different path: it has risen in every one of the eleven weeks since W31, from €1.518 to €1.862 by W41 (+22.7%), with no pullback yet, including a +2.7% jump in the most recent week alone (W40 to W41). Basilicata topping out in mid-September while the rest of the country keeps climbing is the single most interesting fuel trend in today's data.

network_section.heading: 267 Registered Stations, 239 Reporting: A Solid but Imperfect Picture
paragraphs: Basilicata has 267 registered fuel stations in the MIMIT registry as of today, of which 239 reported prices — a reporting rate of 89.5%. That is a modest step below the national reporting rate of 90.6% (21,684 of 23,930 registered stations), but close enough that Basilicata's regional averages should be read with roughly the same confidence as the national figures.

The station count itself has been fairly stable over the tracked period, hovering in the 267-270 range with small month-to-month fluctuations — 267 as of July 21, rising to a high of 270 in mid-September, back to 267 today — normal churn as individual stations register, deregister, or temporarily stop reporting rather than any structural shift in the region's fuel retail network.

methodology_section.heading: Built to Run Itself: No Analyst, No Spreadsheet
paragraphs: Everything in this report — the daily MIMIT data pull, the region-of-the-day rotation, the weekly trend analysis, and the prose you're reading right now — is produced automatically every morning by an unattended pipeline built with Claude Code, Anthropic's coding agent. No person picks the region, builds the charts, or writes the commentary; the pipeline fetches the latest registry and price files, computes the weekly aggregates for the featured region and for Italy as a whole, and an AI agent turns those numbers into this write-up, end to end, without manual intervention.

That is a deliberate contrast with how a project like this is usually run: as a spreadsheet someone updates by hand, with charts that go stale the week the analyst gets busy. Automating the whole chain — ingestion, analysis, and writing — means the dashboard and this report stay current every single day, cover a different one of Italy's 20 regions on a fixed rotation so none gets ignored, and free up the time a manual process would have spent on upkeep instead of on deciding what the trend actually means.

closing.heading: Explore Beyond Basilicata

From there, use the scope picker to switch to Region, Province, Municipality, or a different Operator/Brand and dig into whichever slice of the market you actually care about, whether that is your own town or a competitor's pricing.

pull_quote: National Metano prices have risen for eleven straight weeks; Basilicata's peaked in mid-September and have fallen for three weeks running.
caption:
Today's regional spotlight on Fuel Dashboard: Basilicata — and the standout number is Metano. While the national self-service Metano price has climbed for eleven straight weeks (up 22.7% since late July), Basilicata's own Metano price peaked back in mid-September and has now fallen for three weeks running, down 7.2% from that peak. Everything else in the region — Benzina, Gasolio, GPL — is running close to the national average, but Metano is quietly moving in the opposite direction from the rest of the country.

Fuel Dashboard tracks daily fuel prices across all 23,930+ registered stations in Italy, by region, province, municipality, and brand, and publishes a fresh deep-dive report on a different region every day. Today's report on Basilicata is live now.

The part I think is actually interesting here isn't the fuel prices — it's how this gets made. There's no analyst pulling MIMIT's daily CSV exports, no one updating a spreadsheet, no one picking which region to cover or writing up what the numbers mean. Claude Code runs the entire pipeline every morning: pulling the data, picking the day's region on a fixed rotation, computing the weekly trends, writing the report, and publishing it — unattended. A year ago this would have been a part-time job for someone. Today it's a script and an AI agent that doesn't take a day off. If you're still maintaining something like this by hand in Excel, it's worth asking how much of that could just run itself.
